11.2701: Dragon Age: The Veilguard — A Masterpiece That Trips Over Itself - Probably the best game in the series mechanically. Possibly the most frustrating to recommend. Some classes need rebalancing, but for a single-player game that's a minor footnote, not a dealbreaker. RPG and Story - Your decisions carry weight — genuinely Game of Thrones-level weight in places. You can't play a villain, but that's true of most BioWare titles and rarely a problem. The companion system is strong: each character has a real backstory, personality, and arc. Voice acting is excellent across the board. The story has some genuinely surprising moments, and while map reuse for story missions gets tedious, the world is large enough that it doesn't become suffocating. Where It Falls Apart: Immersion - The biggest bug in this game isn't performance or writing.

11.2626: 그냥 '베일가드'로 나왔다면 괜찮은 게임이다. 살짝 부족한 A급정도? 하지만 슬프게도 이 게임은 '드래곤 에이지™:베일가드'로 나왔다. 그리고 이것이 '복합적'인 심정의 비추천의 원인이다. 평가를 쓸려면 어쨌든 한 번은 엔딩을 봐야된다고 생각해서 세일가에 구매하여 1회차를 돌렸다. 어느정도 성실하게 돌아서 '진엔딩'이라고 부르는 결말을 봤다. 그리고 나도 복합적인 심정이 되었다. 어디서 읽었는데 제대로 플레이 해보지도 않고 몇몇 트레일러와 스크린샷 및 기사를 보고 냅다 욕부터 박는다고 하던데 이것은 잘 모르고 하는 소리다. 플레이하는 내내 이게 내가 플레이하던 오리진, 2, 인퀴지션을 잇는 드래곤 에이지가 맞는지 의문이 들었다. 매번 시리즈가 발매될때마다 게임형태가 확확 바뀐건 맞았지만 이건 스타일정도가 바뀐게 아니라 뭐라 말을해야될까 어. 시발 친자검사를 해봐야하지 않을까? 어디서 혼종새끼하나 델구와서 니새끼라고 빡빡우기는데 이 애새끼가 좋은애인지 나쁜애인지 잘생긴애인지 못생긴애인지 봐달라는 게 뭔 개소린가? 바로 친자검사하자 소리밖에 안나오는 것이다. 발매직전부터 초기에 정신줄 놓은듯한 악플과 서글픈 악플이 주르륵 달린 이유가 바로 이런 이유때문이 아닐까? 이게 그 드래곤에이지™ 라고? 더구나 꼴에 "드래곤에이지"처럼 보이겠답시고 전작 설정 몇을 꾸깃꾸깃 구겨넣은게 더 빡치게 만들었을지도 모르겠다. 여러가지 내부사정들이 있었고 나름 최선으로 매듭지었다고 말할 수도 있지만 이렇게 나와서는 안되는 거였다. 이걸 드래곤에이지라고 하면 안되는 거였다. 아직 발매 후 1년도 안 지났지만 이미 오래전 망한 왕국의 폐허를 보는 기분을 지울 수 없다. 폐허에서 왕국이 기적적으로 재건될 일도 없어보인다. 내 앞의 무수한 비추천의 이유와 심정을 충분히 공감하기에 나도 복합적인 마음으로 비추천을 한다. 11.23699: Overall, the core mechanics were engaging and the world was enchanting enough to keep me coming back night after night. 11.23700: Dragon Age: The Veilguard is a true tour de force from a company that knew it had to give its all to stay relevant thirty years after its founding—and it has undoubtedly succeeded.
11.23701: Is this that amazing Dragon Age game we've been waiting years for? No, it's not. Is it a good game? Debatable. But it does so many right things at a few vital points that it managed to win my heart with those moments alone.
11.23702: Regardless of the developers' goals, Veilguard feels like a game designed and assembled in parts. However good any idea, scene or concept is - and there are some excellent ones - it isn't bolstered by those beside it. Instead, each feels like a dazzling distraction from where it falls short in depth, consistency and trust in players to engage with a complex world. [Issue#405, p.102]
11.23703: The party members are a delight to spend time with and woo. The combat is some of the most fun I’ve had in a while with an action RPG. It is just a shame everything else falls short. The exploration is far too uninteresting, the story is haphazardly put together, and the mission structure is too linear. There is a good enough RPG to enjoy in Dragon Age: The Veilguard for diehard fans like myself, but this is certainly no second coming of BioWare. I have disliked each new Dragon Age more than the previous one and, unfortunately, The Veilguard continues that.
11.23704: BioWare's worst dialog, trivial puzzles, annoying level design, and tedious combat. My diagnosis: complete apathy.

20.4871: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a story-driven action-adventure set in the aftermath of Order 66, following former Padawan Cal Kestis as he is forced out of hiding and drawn into a conflict with the Empire. While the story is not especially groundbreaking and several developments are fairly predictable, the game succeeds through its emotional sincerity, cinematic presentation, and strong sense of adventure. At its core, the game allows players to explore a series of interconnected planets, progress through a linear main story, solve environmental puzzles, and return to earlier areas after unlocking new abilities. 20.4752: [h1]새로운 제다이의 탄생[/h1] 기존 스타워즈 게임 시리즈의 핵앤슬래쉬에서 벗어나 [b]소울라이크 장르를 도입한 새로운 시리즈의 시작[/b], [b]Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order(스타워즈 제다이: 오더의 몰락)[/b]입니다. 플레이어는 66호 명령 이후 간신히 살아남은 젊은 파다완 [b]칼 케스티스[/b]가 되어, 5년간의 은둔 생활이 발각되며 제국의 추적을 피해 제다이 오더를 재건하기 위한 여정을 떠나게 됩니다. [hr][/hr] [h2]전투와 탐험[/h2] 전투는 소울라이크 스타일을 차용하여 체력 관리, 패링, 스태미너 기반의 공격 타이밍이 핵심입니다. 라이트세이버의 무게감과 타격감은 매우 뛰어나며, 싱글 블레이드 듀얼 블레이드 이도류 등 여러 공격 방식을 활용할 수 있고, 각 적 유형마다 패턴을 읽어 대응하는 재미가 있습니다. 포스를 이용한 밀기, 끌기, 정지 등의 능력은 전투와 퍼즐 양쪽에 유기적으로 활용되며, [b]메트로배니아 형식의 레벨 디자인[/b]으로 초반에는 갈 수 없던 지역을 후반 능력 해금 후 다시 탐험하게 만드는 구조가 탐색 욕구를 자극합니다. [hr][/hr] [h2]연출과 분위기[/h2] 그래픽과 연출은 매우 시네마틱하게 구현되어 스타워즈 팬이라면 높은 몰입감을 느낄 수 있습니다. 주인공 칼 케스티스를 연기한 [b]캐머런 모나한[/b]의 연기는 이야기에 생동감을 더해주는 중요한 요소이며, 후반부의 [spoiler]다스 베이더 등장 연출[/spoiler]은 기존 팬들 사이에서도 특히 호평을 받았습니다. [hr][/hr] [h2]아쉬운 점[/h2] 스타워즈 세계관에 익숙하지 않은 플레이어에게는 각 행성의 배경이나 역사적 맥락이 다소 불친절하게 느껴질 수 있습니다. “이 행성은 왜 이렇게 황폐해졌지?” “저 인물은 왜 나에게 적대적인 거지?” 같은 의문이 충분한 설명 없이 남기도 합니다. 또한 후반부에 합류하는 동료 [b]메린[/b]의 경우, 동료가 되는 과정과 동기가 조금은 급하게 느껴지는 점이 아쉬웠습니다.

20.24059: Fallen Order is a must have for Star Wars fans and the best Star Wars game in years. Both literally and figuratively: the Force is strong with this one. [01/2020, p.42]

20.24061: An excellent entry into the new Star Wars canon.
20.24062: Fallen Order is a decent alternative to Dark Souls if you’re looking for a less hardcore experience. 20.24063: As underwhelmed as I was by Fallen Order, I hope that its inevitable success will encourage EA to do more with this franchise, since it makes a powerful case for the resonance of Star Wars — if this mediocre casserole of concepts yanked from superior titles didn’t have the license attached, I doubt anyone would be talking about it.
20.24064: With Jedi Fallen Order, Respawn have made a small miracle and have delivered a stellar single-player Star Wars game. 20.24065: Technical issues marr an otherwise slick adventure. A must for Star Wars fans.
20.24066: With an excellent droid companion and entertaining lightsaber combat, Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order could have been a truly forceful addition to the franchise. However, navigation problems and unnatural level design takes it back down a darker path.
20.24067: Being an EA game, albeit developed by Respawn Entertainment, I had some doubts, but they were quickly dispelled. It stands as proof that single-player games can stand on their own. The only problem is that if you rush through it, you could finish Fallen Order in about 12 hours, but that excludes finding the secrets and unlocking all the cool stuff. Lastly, I have to mention the name, Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order. To me, it sounds like Star Wars Jedi could be a new line of games, with Fallen Order being just the first one. We can only dream.
20.24068: Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order is yet another excellent game developed by Respawn. 20.24069: Although lacking in innovation, Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is the best Star Wars game of all time.
20.24070: Fallen Order is a game whose worst moments are serviceable, and best moments are memorable. It’s worth experiencing by Star Wars fans hungry for an original story that doesn’t settle for trite, and action game players looking for a decent – albeit flawed – combat.
20.24071: Jedi: Fallen Order borrows liberally from other games, but a strong supporting cast, clever level design, and a cute little droid companion make Respawn's Star Wars story more than the sum of its parts.
20.24072: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order certainly tries, but as Yoda pointed out, you either do or do not. For the most part, it does -- but without the grace or precision of a full-fledged Jedi Knight. The apprentice is not yet the master.
20.24073: Falling Order mixes acrobatics with exploration and challenging light saber battles. Excessive enemy respawns and unnecessary backtracking reduce the enjoyment, though.
20.24074: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order could have been a good, short, but intense action game, lasting about ten hours, but instead, it swallows the player in unnecessary back and forths, artificial obstacles, puzzles and chests hunts, which burden the rhythm and fun. We come out all the more frustrated by a predictable story that goes nowhere, as well as by its combat system very close to Sekiro's, but which is far from reaching its level of refinement and control, especially on the bosses.
20.24075: Respawn did nothing to reinvent the wheel, but instead married a bunch of popular gameplay genres together into a cohesive whole, wrapped up in well-crafted Star Wars story. It may not be KOTOR levels of greatness, but it's good. And I think that's exactly what fans needed right about now.
20.24076: I was astonished at how much I enjoyed Jedi Fallen Order. Not because it’s a great game, it inhabits a niche that we haven’t seen much of this generation. It’s merely a good game. I ran into a ton of glitches and collision issues. Still, the overall package was entertaining enough to ignore them for the most part.
20.24077: Fallen Order wants you to feel like a fighty, telepathic space priest, and for about 20 hours or so, it does that. Stick with it, and you might also find a cool, yellow lightsaber.
20.24078: Gameplay is solid from the start and gains depth, transforming you into a Jedi badass. Respawn has also nailed the Star Wars universe, for better (sights, sounds, and cinematic flair) and worse (cringey dialogue and vacuous plot).
20.24079: It's good enough that its host of technical problems feels like an affront to what the game could have been, and to the hard work and talent--and there's a considerable amount of talent here--of the people who made it.
20.24080: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order hits the target by offering the right mix of adrenaline-pumping action and thoughtful exploration. The metroidvania mechanics are grafted to perfection within the game formula, and the same can be said for those borrowed from the latest productions of From Software. 20.24087: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order makes up for a lot of lost time with a fantastic single-player action-adventure that marks the return of the playable Jedi.
20.24081: I love Star Wars, I love video games, and Fallen Order is a glorious amalgamation of the two. 20.24082: Much like what Arkham Asylum did for Batman games, Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order sets the new standard for Star Wars titles. Not only is it a great Star Wars game, it is also the best game of the year.
20.24083: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is the ideal example of a Star Wars game in 2019. It's an expert blend of multiple genres.
20.24084: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is an absolute masterpiece. Well paced, written, and executed, the game is Respawn’s best thus far.
20.24085: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is the Star Wars game that fans have been crying out for years now. 20.24086: Thanks to a mix-and-match of different genres Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is the best Star Wars-game is years. 20.24088: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order captured the magic of growing as a Jedi, overcoming insurmountable odds through fellowship, and the power of hope in the midst of despair. 20.24089: Despite its polish and best ideas, I wish I'd just reinstalled both Force Unleashed games, and I encourage anybody eager for a fun, Force-filled, third-person Star Wars experience this year to do the same.
20.24090: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a dream come true for many Star Wars fans. It perfectly combines great gameplay with exploration, puzzles and a personal story. Sadly a lackluster ending and some technical and graphical issues tarnish the overall positive experience somewhat.
20.24091: Developer Respawn builds a Star Wars adventure that constantly reminds me why I fell in love with the Skywalker saga as a child. Fallen Order is a love letter to the classic trilogy, respects the clone wars, and shows me the dark era of the Empire like no other Star Wars story before.
20.24092: I greatly enjoyed my time playing Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order. 32.7553: 안녕하세요? 플스 5로 먼저 즐기다가, PC에서도 하고 싶어서 이번에 다시 구매해 봤습니다. 많은 사람들이 이 게임을 “쿠팡맨”이라고 부르지만, 그 한 단어로는 데스 스트랜딩을 다 담기 어렵다고 느꼈어요. 게임이 시작하자마자 우리에게 요구하는 건 사실 단순합니다. “이 물건을 짊어지고 목적지까지 배달해라.” 딱 이거 하나요. 그런데 그 단순한 행동을 몇 시간만 따라가다 보면, 어느 순간 ‘걷는 행위’ 자체가 감정이 되고 서사가 되는 순간이 확 찾아옵니다. 몰입감이 장난 아니에요. 게임의 핵심은 결국 짐과 지형입니다. 화물이 무거울수록, 지형이 험할수록 배달은 훨씬 까다로워지고, 조금만 중심을 잃어도 짐이 한꺼번에 우르르 쏟아집니다. 강과 절벽을 피해 길을 고르고, 우회로를 만들고, 매 순간 “어떻게 건너갈까”를 판단하게 되죠. 단순히 이동하는 게 아니라, 한 발 한 발이 선택이 됩니다. 비동기 온라인 시스템도 정말 매력적입니다. 누군가 미리 설치해둔 발전기나 도로, 표지판을 마주칠 때마다 “나 혼자 하는 게임이 아닌가?” 싶은 착각이 들 정도로 연결감이 좋아요. 직접 만나진 않지만, 쌓여가는 좋아요를 보면 괜히 기분이 좋아집니다. 히히. 연출과 스토리는 스포가 될까 봐 길게 말하진 않겠지만… 솔직히 이걸 게임이 아니라 소설로 읽어보고 싶다는 생각을 했어요. 그만큼 설정과 이야기 자체가 매력적입니다. 단점. 초반 템포가 너~무 느려서 진짜 답답할 수 있어요. 근데 이건 템포가 빨라 질수록 내가 이 세상을 정리해 나간다는 느낌이 들어서 성취감이 더 커지긴 해요. UI가 조금 복잡하고, 처음엔 익숙해지는 데 시간이 걸립니다. 그럼에도 불구하고, 이 게임은 단순한 “배달”을 특별한 경험으로 바꿔버리는 힘이 있는 작품이었습니다. 느린 호흡을 견디기만 하면, 분명히 한 번쯤은 “아, 이게 데스 스트랜딩이지” 하는 순간이 옵니다. + 코지마 너 연출의 신이냐? 총점 ★☆/★ (4.0)

32.32065: "멸종은 기회야, 샘." 게임은 메인/섭 배달 퀘스트로 이루어져있다. 메인만 밀어도 스토리가 완료되지만, 섭 퀘를 해야 장비 업그레이드를 시켜주는 경우가 많고, 자원도 얻을 수 있다. 처음에는 장비가 없기 때문에, 배달이 조금 난감하게 느껴질 수도 있지만 맵 디자인과 중간중간 나오는 음악들이 상당히 아름답기 때문에 즐기면서 천천히 배달하면 좋다. 나중에는 여러 구조물과 장비를 지어 순식간에 이동이 가능하기 때문에, 수월한 배달이 가능하다. ex) 조금만 지나면 이동수단을 탈 수 있다. 그리고, 모션캡쳐로 만든 실제 배우들(노먼 리더스, 레아 세이두, 매즈 미캘슨 등)이 출연하기 때문에, 그 배우들을 알거나 팬이라면 하라고 추천하고 싶다. 셋 다 잘 알고 좋아하던 배우들이였기에, 글쓴이는 출시 전 부터 하고싶어했다. 요새 50% 가까이 세일을 많이 하기 때문에, 세일 구간을 노려보는게 좋다고 생각한다. ※ 디렉터스 컷 또한 존재하는데, 더 다양한 장비를 사용할 수 있고, 짧지만 엑스트라 스토리가 있다. 전투가 초반에는 많지 않고 피해야 하는 경우가 많지만, 갈수록 전투장비 또한 다양하게 얻을 수 있고, 강력해지기 때문에 처음에는 비중이 작은 전투가 나중에는 갈수록 조금씩 커지기 시작한다. 스토리 부분은 이해가 되면서도 잘 안되는 듯한 그런 느낌을 풍기며, 아예 난해하진 않다. 천천히 빠져들게 되는 매력이 있는 세계관이라고 말할 수 있겠다. 스토리도 에피소드 형식으로 되있고, 에피소드마다 게임 내 특정 캐릭터에 관한 내용이 나온다. 마지막으로 갈 수록, 몰입이 잘 되도록 설계 되어있다. 또, npc들이 메일을 보내면서 추후에 어떻게 지내는 지도 꾸준히 연락이 오기 때문에, 마치 정말 살아있는 느낌도 살짝 든다. (또, 나중에 어떤 식으로 지내는 지 그런 식으로 알려준다.) 세계관 및 설정에 관한 것은, 에피소드 진행마다 얻게 되는 정보란 (npc 인터뷰 내용) 에서 더 자세하게 읽어 볼 수 있다.

34.7998: 《A Plague Tale: Innocence》 was far more enjoyable than I originally expected. At first, I thought it would be a slow-paced medieval adventure focused mainly on storytelling. However, the actual pacing turned out to be much more intense and engaging. The frequent chase sequences, stealth pressure, and constant threat of the rat swarms kept the tension high throughout the game, so it rarely felt dragged out. The story was also much more interesting than I anticipated. What begins as a grounded tale set during the Black Death gradually evolves into something involving religious fanaticism, alchemy, bloodline curses, and supernatural elements. While some parts of the lore are never fully explained, that ambiguity actually adds to the mysterious atmosphere. The emotional relationship between the brother and sister was handled very well, and it genuinely made me want to keep following their journey to the end.

34.8000: A shorter, medieval French take on The Last of Us — but with rats. My only real complaint is that the latter half forces you into direct combat and kills, removing the stealth options that were available in the first half. The dark world of medieval France combined with excellent presentation and the story of Amicia de Rune protecting her younger brother in a brutal world filled with death and chaos, makes the game immediately engaging. The gameplay itself isn’t particularly challenging — the game often guides the player — but this feels intentional. The real focus is on the narrative, the emotions and the relationships between the characters. At its core, it’s a story about loyalty, growing up and discovering that family can also be the people you meet along the way.
34.8076: It's a good game and I did enjoy it. The story is unique that keeps you engaged. Voice acting, music and graphics are great. It has emotional and touching moments. The game has bugs, so anytime you come across one or get stuck, just set the resolution scale to 200% under graphics setting. Thank me later. The game is generally easy, but there is a difficulty spike during the last chapter or two. I'd recommend this game, maybe more so if it's on sale.
34.8080: very unique and good game. journey was fun and emotional, i really liked it, now time to rush for its requiem.
34.8075: A Plague Tale: Innocence is a truly memorable experience that left a strong impression on me. The game features beautiful graphics that perfectly capture the dark, medieval atmosphere of France infected by plague. Every location feels detailed and alive, despite the overwhelming sense of danger. What really stands out is the incredible atmosphere. The constant tension, enhanced by the haunting music, keeps you fully engaged from start to finish. The voice acting is absolutely amazing, it’s emotional and believable which makes it easy to connect with the characters, especially Amicia. The story is interesting and well-written, mixing personal drama with historical horror in a way that feels fresh. I also really enjoyed the stealth mechanics, which are so good designed that neutralizing targets felt rewarding. Also sneaking past enemies, using light, shadows, and the environment made every encounter feel intense. Most importantly, I had a great time playing this game.

34.7937: ▷평점 : ★ A Plague Tale : Innocence 2019년 6월 4일에 출시한, 1인칭 시네마틱 어드벤처 게임. 다른 의미로 공포 게임이며, 잠입 탈출에 가까운 게임이다. 먼저 이 게임을 하기 전에 역사를 알 필요가 있다. 이 게임은 14세기 프랑스와 잉글랜드 간에 전쟁이 발발했던 '백년 전쟁'을 배경으로 만들어졌다. '프랑스 왕위 계승 분쟁'이라고 말할 수 있는 이 전쟁은, 무려 116년간 전쟁을 했던 역사적 사건이다. 여기서 잉글랜드와 영국을 헛갈리는 사람들이 있을 텐데, 영국은 '잉글랜드', '스코틀랜드', '웨일스', '북아일랜드' 이렇게 4개의 지역의 연합 국가이며, 당시 잉글랜드는 영국과는 상관없는 별개의 왕권 중 하나였다. 각설하고, 당시 프랑스를 통치하던 '카페 직계'의 마지막 왕인 '샤를 4세'가 사망하게 되면서 최초 갈등이 시작되었다. (*1328년) 직계 계승자가 없는 프랑스 왕권은 왕위 계승자를 찾기 시작했고, 왕위 계승권으로 우선순위에 있던 잉글랜드의 국왕(에드워드 3세)의 어머니인 '이사벨라'는 여성이라는 이유로 프랑스 왕위를 요구할 수 없게되자, 자신의 아들(에드워드 3세)를 프랑스 왕위 계승으로 주장했다. (*이사벨라는 프랑스 전대 국왕(필리프 4세)의 딸이며, 사망한 프랑스 왕(샤를 4세)의 친누나이다) 하지만, 프랑스 의회에서는 애초에 여성으로서 왕위 계승권을 요구할 수 없으므로, 당연히 아들 또한 계승권이 없다고 못을 박았다. 그렇게 '카페' 핏줄의 '방계'(발루아가 핏줄)가 프랑스 왕위를 계승하게 된다. 그리고 9년 뒤, (*1337년) 잉글랜드와 스코틀랜드 간의 전쟁이 발생하였고, 프랑스의 국왕(방계 출신 - 필리프6세)은 잉글랜드를 도와주기는커녕 스코틀랜드 편을 들어주기 시작했다. 이 사건 때문에 다시금 프랑스와 잉글랜드간에 갈등이 시작되었고, 잉글랜드에서 프랑스 왕위를 다시 요구하게 된다. 당연히 프랑스 왕권은 반대를 하게 되고, 마침내 프랑스와 잉글랜드간에 최초 전쟁이 시작되었다.

34.24615: One of my favorite moments is when Amicia spots another wildflower in a lone trek across the city, nestled among the decay of the rats’ revolting nests. Despite flashes of predictability, moments like these will bring a lump to your throat, as it did mine.

There are kinks here and there in the story, which is a little bloated, but this is easily forgivable - they were trying to make the package as full as possible. Given the wealth of things to do, the fun gameplay, and the engrossing story that can be as straightforward or as deep as you want, depending on what you do, this is a game that you owe yourself to play, and one of the rare games that is worth its full price. [h1]훌륭한 수미상관[/h1] 유럽 신화의 시작과 끝을 관통하며, 크레토스의 신으로서의 고뇌와 아버지로서의 성장을 완벽에 가까운 수미상관으로 마무리 지었습니다. 전작에서 뿌려둔 복선들을 회수하며 '피로 얼룩진 과거'를 뒤로하고 새로운 길을 제시하는 서사는 묵직한 감동을 줍니다. 한 시대를 풍미한 주인공에게 이보다 더 깔끔하고 명예로운 예우가 있을까 싶을 정도로 서사가 정교합니다. [h1]웅장한 액션 시퀀스 연출[/h1] 게임 시작부터 입에서 '개쩐다'라는 소리가 절로 나옵니다. 압도적인 스케일의 연출과 화면을 가득 채우는 박진감은 소니 퍼스트 파티 게임의 저력을 다시 한번 증명하죠. 여기에 상황에 맞춰 몰입감을 극대화하는 웅장한 OST까지 한몫 거들면서, 패드를 잡고 있는 내내 블록버스터 영화의 한복판에 서 있는 듯한 전율을 느끼게 합니다. [h1]갓 오브 퍼즐[/h1] 전작의 퍼즐 요소가 그렇게들 재밌다고 리뷰를 남기셨는지, 이번 작에도 아주 낭낭하게 퍼즐을 때려 박아놨습니다. 메인 길을 뚫을 때도 퍼즐, 히든 요소를 찾을 때도 퍼즐입니다. 신나게 몹들을 패다가 고요한 필드에서 혼자 도끼 던지고 도르래 돌리고 있으면 현타가 제대로 옵니다.

[b]장점[/b] [list] [*] 환골탈태한 최적화와 버그 수정: HITMAN 출시 당시엔 최적화 이슈를 비롯해 온갖 버그들이 난무했지만, 브랜드 통합 이후 HITMAN3까지 오면서 버그 수정은 물론 최적화도 훌륭하게 잘 잡았다. [*] 초심자를 위한 배려: 다소 복잡할 수 있는 잠입과 암살 시스템을 튜토리얼을 통해 초심자들도 쉽게 적응할 수 있도록 보다 잘 다듬었다. [*] 압도적인 볼륨과 리플레이성: 변장, 사고 위장 등 다양한 루트로 타겟을 암살하는 자유도가 매우 우수하다. 로그라이크 요소를 결합한 프리랜서 모드 등 지속적인 라이브 콘텐츠 업데이트로 파고들 요소가 넘쳐난다. [*] 획기적인 용량 압축: 3개의 게임 분량을 하나로 통합했음에도 엔진 개선과 에셋 중복을 줄여 전체 설치 용량을 획기적으로 줄인 기술력은 상당히 만족스럽다. [/list] [b]단점[/b] [list] [*] 기만적인 과금 모델: 히트맨 1과 2를 기존에 소유했던 유저라 하더라도, 2편의 확장팩 지역과 3편 콘텐츠에 접근하려면 액세스 패스 명목으로 디럭스 팩을 강제로 구매해야 한다. 기존 구매자 입장에서는 불합리한 이중 지출로 느껴진다. [*] 혼란스러운 에디션 구분: 상점에서 판매되는 Part One이나 일반판을 간보기용으로 구매할 경우, 온전한 콘텐츠를 즐기기 위해 결국 디럭스 팩을 추가로 결제하게 되어 구매 혼선을 유발한다. [*] 공식 한국어 미지원: 방대한 텍스트와 스토리 비중에도 불구하고 HITMAN 브랜드 통합 이후에도 공식 한글화를 지원하지 않아 언어 장벽이 존재한다. 원활한 플레이를 위해서는 유저 한글패치를 따로 찾아 적용해야 하는 번거로움이 따른다.

49.25223: Hitman: World of Assassination brings together most of the trilogy’s content in a convenient package. 49.25224: Hitman’s Freelancer mode is something rare: an intoxicating blend of challenge and approachability. It plays on the hubris of longtime players, but also guides newcomers with thematic objectives and a more explicit overall structure. It may not allow for the micro-repetition that makes the base trilogy tick. But it does maintain a rapid momentum from the beginning of each run to its bitter, comical end. After so many hours spent with this trilogy, combing each of its locations for something, anything I missed, I did not think it possible for IO to surprise me anymore — but here we are.
49.25225: With any roguelike game, the biggest problem is repetition. If someone has yet to play the recent entries, and with all three previous games wrapped up in one package, Hitman: World of Assassination is an incredible deal. As a free update for players who already own Hitman 3, it's absolutely worth jumping back into.

59.25609: Monster Hunter Rise is a brilliant addition to the Monster Hunter lineup. It delivers incredible combat with newly added monsters and highly-desired mobility. 59.25610: Monster Hunter Rise’s combat is excellent, and the PC version is virtually a perfect port of the Switch version. As someone who had never played a Monster Hunter game before, I’m hooked.
59.25611: Monster Hunter Rise on PC is the definitive version of an excellent entry in this long running franchise and whether you are a veteran of the series or a rookie, looking to jump in for the first time, it’s the perfect opportunity to grab a weapon and start hunting some monsters.
59.25612: The PC port for Monster Hunter Rise is the definitive way to experience this game. I am excited to see where the franchise goes from here, although I will find it hard to slide back into any Monster Hunter game without the new traversal and streamlined elements. Whether you want to hunt alone or play with your friends, play “Fashion Hunter” or experience the main quests, there is something for everyone in Monster Hunter Rise.
59.25613: Monster Hunter is a series about systems—Capcom can’t escape that, no matter how much marketing and PR they throw at it. But it isn’t a series about getting it either, as much as its staunchest adherents would have you believe. It’s about feeling it. And Monster Hunter Rise feels good—simple as that.
59.25614: When considering the PC version of Rise, it’s hard not to compare it directly to the as-yet unmatched juggernaut that is Monster Hunter World – a competition that I don’t think Rise wins. That said, Monster Hunter Rise is still an enjoyable, well-crafted game with some compelling innovations that make it a wonderful addition to the Monster Hunter franchise. Plus, you can make a fire-breathing T-Rex suplex a dragon. If that doesn’t persuade you, nothing will.
59.25615: Monster Hunter Rise remains a stellar title on the PC, hardly losing any ground from the greatness it already achieved earlier this year on the Nintendo Switch. The game looks better than ever now that powerful hardware improves the graphics, giving everything from the monsters to the environments a nice polish. Unfortunately, however, the new format doesn’t always take the various kinds of players into account. Veteran players will likely grow tired of skipping through the tutorials again, and any player not set up with the right controls will be missing out somewhat. Anyone who has been patient enough to wait, or doesn’t own a Nintendo Switch, will be happy to have an overall superior version.
59.25616: Monster Hunter Rise stands toe-to-toe with World, especially on PC. Its end-game grind may not be as robust, but a serious focus on fun and community over narrative and fidelity pays off.
59.25617: The PC version of Monster Hunter Rise is a solid port that in general does not differ much from what we saw on Switch. Therefore, praise and complaints about the Switch edition mostly still apply. It’s a bit disappointing that the year that has passed between the releases brought us little more than graphical improvements, but the game itself is still stellar.
59.25618: With an accelerated combat system, some light grind and well-designed monsters, Monster Hunter Rise will provide you with many hours of adrenaline-filled fun. The experience that this game provides in multiplayer is unique, regardless of the complicated formation of the party. Definitely a version that every PC gamer should have in their Steam library.
59.25619: Monster Hunter Rise blends the best elements from earlier series entries, and delivers a streamlined, action-packed, monster-slaying experience.
59.25620: I strongly recommend Monster Hunter Rise, but this isn’t World. It’s harder, less environmentally appealing, and more focused on the rivalry between the hunters and the monsters. Gaining the pieces to build that armor or make that weapon is sometimes a bit more of a grind as the RNG isn’t quite as good but the satisfaction as always is there and strong. But amazing combat and great rewards keep the fun moving, albeit very differently from its most recent predecessor.
59.25621: Monster Hunter Rise combines all of the quality of life features introduced in World while keeping the best parts of the earlier games in the series, resulting in the most refined Monster Hunter title to date.
59.25622: Despite releasing nearly a year after its Switch counterpart, the PC version of Monster Hunter Rise feels like a minimal improvement. Sure, you can get frame rates in the hundreds and high resolutions, but frequent crashes can reset your settings and cutscenes are still locked at 30. The keyboard and mouse control options are a big boon for accessibility, but the visual improvements here feel so minimal I’ll stick to the portable edition.
59.25623: Monster Hunter Rise has lost none of its appeal in moving from a Nintendo Switch screen to a PC one. In Ultrawide, with an unlocked frame-rate, it’s the best way to play what may be the franchise’s best entry yet. If you’re looking for deep RPG systems, a T-Rex that breathes fire, and a huge hammer to smack it in the head with, then Monster Hunter Rise is essential.
59.25624: Indeed, although it is identical in terms of content to the Nintendo Switch version on PC, it is a total success and remains an excellent gateway for beginners.
59.25625: Monster Hunter Rise is probably the best game in the series. It isn’t quite as accessible as World, but long term it offers much more varied combat and a richer experience. If you have a choice, it’s definitely the way to play, the best and most complete version of one of 2021’s standout games.
59.25626: Monster Hunter Rise isn’t as ambitious as its predecessor, but it still manages to build on the franchise in meaningful ways.
59.25627: Monster Hunter Rise is a big step forward for the Monster Hunter series, both in terms of its design and the quality of its PC port. The port is nothing groundbreaking, but the MH team has done themselves proud with this, and I’m just glad to be able to play this game at a high framerate.
59.25628: Beyond mounting monsters and using the wirebug to wall-run in spectacular fashion, not much else distinguishes Monster Hunter Rise from the installments that came before. Monster Hunter Rise is far from being the next definitive chapter in the series. Nevertheless, if you’re looking for a polished-but-conventional adventure with a few small-scale nuances, then you’ll be right at home in Kamura Village.

59.25635: Monster Hunter Rise is a great game that’s even better on PC, but it’s hard to recommend if you’ve already played it on the Switch and don’t have unlimited free time. If you managed to get a Steam Deck preorder, though, this could well be the perfect game to christen it with for anyone looking to get into the series. It’s just unfortunate that Monster Hunter enthusiasts who already jumped on Rise will have to start from scratch. I hope Capcom releases future Monster Hunter games on PC at the same time as consoles, or finds a way to include cross-save functionality — ideally both.
59.25642: Monster Hunter Rise on PC is the best place to play this incredible creature battler. If the series was looking for a permanent home, PC players would be more than happy to see it moving in.
59.25636: Monster Hunter Rise arrives on PC in dazzling form, complete with support for 4K resolution, unlocked frame-rate and ultrawide monitors. Too bad we’re not able to carry the old save into this new version that will force you to start all over again.
59.25637: An excellent port that presents a solid, complete experience. Super fast load times, improved performance and a ton of content make Monster Hunter Rise on PC the definitive version.
59.25638: Monster Hunter Rise is at its best on the PC. The extra power brings a smoother, prettier experience to an already cracking game.
59.25639: Monster Hunter Rise looks better on PC, runs better on PC, has more control & online options on PC, and arrives with more content at its respective launch.
59.25640: Overall, Monster Hunter Rise on PC is another perfect example of why the series belongs on computer. It offers all the excellent experiences found on the Nintendo Switch, albeit with improved visuals, better resolution, a myriad of performance options, and greater controller support. Hopefully there comes a day when PC players get to experience a Monster Hunter title at the same time as console players, because the series has shown that it thrives on PC, with a playerbase ready to dive into it with their whole hearts. For those that have been biding their time, I’m pleased to say that Monster Hunter Rise on PC has been well worth the wait.
59.25641: Monster Hunter Rise on PC has all the updates and new content added to the Switch version right from the get go with vastly improved performance and graphics. While the visuals could've been improved further, this is still the best way to play Monster Hunter Rise.
59.25643: With the streamlining of some of the most annoying aspects of the Monster Hunter experience and some excellent additions to the formula like Wirebugs and Switch Skills, Monster Hunter Rise reaches the heights of the best entries in the series with ease. While not all of the changes and new features have been for the best, like Rampage Quests, their general quality level, and the amazing PC port, do make the game one that's worth playing for both long-time fans of the series and newcomers.
59.25644: For the most part, though, Monster Hunter Rise is another stonking addition to the series, and in my books a more than worthy successor to Monster Hunter: World. There's a generous and playful sense of freedom here that keeps combat and exploration feeling fresh, and the momentum of its hunting-led missions means you're rarely spinning your wheels as you seek out that last elusive armour part. It's kept me playing much longer than I ever did with World, and I can't wait to see how it develops with its imminent Sunbreak expansion later this summer.
59.25645: Overall, the PC port of Monster Hunter Rise is superior to the Nintendo Switch version, thanks to the PC enhancements. It has some of the best combat mechanics in the Monster Hunter series, the new monsters are an absolute delight to hunt, and the improved frame rate and resolutions enrich the hunting experience. It does have a couple of flaws, but they are minor issues in the grand scheme of things.
59.25646: Monster Hunter Rise on PC is just a different way to play a fantastic game. And while that’s great news for PC players who’ve never bought into Nintendo’s ecosystem, its graphics fail to impress, even on the most impressive of hardware.
59.25647: An impressive port, with a good amount of graphical options and great optimization. Indeed the best way to enjoy Rise's amazing combat system.
59.25648: Almost a year after the debut of Monster Hunter Rise on Switch, the expectation of fans on PC has been rewarded with a valuable port, which not only preserves the merits of the original version but enhances them with a good collection of technical improvements. Net of some fluctuations in the overall yield of the proposal, the new edition of Rise therefore has all the credentials to offer the people of Steam dozens of hours of hunting fun and epic clashes, enhanced by an unprecedented fluidity for the Capcom title.
59.25649: This is a fantastic adaptation of a fantastic game, that plays and looks better than ever on PC.
59.25650: Monster Hunter Rise is another entertaining entry in the venerated franchise that continues to scratch a unique itch. New players will be eased into the franchise and returning players will enjoy hunting with friends as well. Capcom has also delivered yet another good port that definitely makes this version the one to play.
59.25651: A hundred hours in, Rise does feel a little rote. The lack of quest variety and endgame options besides grinding for talismans has begun to wear on me somewhat. But the journey of getting to this point has been nothing short of an incredible experience. From zipping through the air to bludgeon monsters in the face to setting out on gathering runs with my trusty palamute, the minute-to-minute gameplay of Rise is impeccable. The only real issue with Rise is that there isn’t more of it, but with plenty of future updates and an entire expansion on the horizon, this is surely just the beginning of what this game has to offer.
59.25652: Thanks to a beautifully realised setting and some genuinely innovative combat additions, Monster Hunter Rise is fun from start to finish. If you haven’t played a Monster Hunter game yet, this is the best one to start with.
59.25653: Monster Hunter Rise is a successful and worthy port, its fantastic gameplay and content more than compensate for the somewhat outdated graphics on PC. It's still clean and rather pleasant to look at during the fights, and especially very fluid. Those who enjoyed Monster Hunter World shouldn't hesitate to jump in, it's an equally valid game in the license, even if it's a bit different. For the others, it's also a gateway to the license, with improvements in comfort and accessibility, as well as a slightly faster pace of play than its predecessors.
59.25654: This PC port fulfills its role very well because it cancels a lot of limitations of the Switch version. The framerate is no longer stuck at 30 frames per second, the resolution can go up to 4K, some textures are much more detailed, and loading times are noticeably reduced. However, we should not expect either that this former Nintendo exclusive will miraculously transform into graphic mastery worthy of the biggest productions of 2022.
59.25655: Monster Hunter: Rise is arguably the greatest entry in Capcom's flagship series, and a game that simply never stops giving.

67.15252: 정말 오랜만에 인생에 남을 게임을 즐기게 되어서 매우 기쁨. 신생 게임 개발사 33명이 만든 작품이 맞나 싶을 정도로 매우 높은 완성도를 가졌으며, 단 한 순간도 게임이 재미없다고 생각된 적이 없을 정도로 재미있었음. 턴제 RPG라는 역사가 깊으면서도 단순하고 지루할 수 있는 이 장르를 새롭게 개척한 점도 대단하다고 생각함. 여러 가지 부분에 대한 나의 의견을 정리해 보았음 1. 스토리/서사 - 취향을 떠나서 서사 자체가 가진 완결성이 매우 높음. 잘 짜여진 몇 권으로 연재된 소설책을 읽는 듯한 느낌이었음. 현실과 동떨어진 SF라고도 할 수 있는 장르임에도 불구하고 초반부터 몰입할 수 있도록 등장인물간의 개연성, 동기를 촘촘하게 잘 만들었다고 생각함. - 특히, 초반 플레이 시점에서 세계관의 새로운 요소들을 이해할 수 있도록 적절한 설명을 다양한 등장인물들로 풀어주었고, 게임 내 환경 곳곳에 배치함으로서 너무 설명적이지 않으면서도 충분히 관심을 가지고 이해를 할 수 있어서 유치하다는 생각을 받지 않았음. - 다만, 처음에 이 게임이 주는 신비로움, 무력함, 공포스러움의 정체가 밝혀지는 후반부의 전개가 다소 개인 혹은 가족의 서사로 집중된다는 점이 아쉽기는 했음. (이 점은 개인의 취향의 영역이라고 생각하기 때문에 개인적인 의견이라는 점을 알아주길 바람) 2. 게임 플레이 (전투) - 이렇게 치열하고 긴장감있는 게임 플레이를 턴제 RPG에서 해볼 수 있다는 점이 놀라움. 나는 스토리와 더불어 매일 경험해야하는 하나하나의 전투 자체가 재미있고 기대되었음. 턴제 RPG 게임의 전투를 이토록 창의적이고 즐겁게 만들어낸 제작자에게 기립 박수를 보내고 싶음 - 우리가 모두 알고 있는 패링, 회피, 기술 등이 존재함에도 불구하고, 이러한 요소들을 33원정대만큼 극적으로 잘 살린 전투가 있을까 싶을 정도임. 웬만한 ARPG의 현장감, 실시간성을 뛰어넘는다고 생각함.

I think by now everyone has played or at least heard about Clair Obscure: Expedition 33, but I'm not going to spoil anything about the game in this review. The story is about a group of people living in a fictional town called Lumiere, inspired by France during the Belle Époque. A huge number can be seen on the monolith that the Paintress paints every year, which affects them, so they form a team of expeditioners to sail to her in hopes of killing her and stopping her from harming the people in Lumiere. This year, Expedition 33 is gathering to start the adventure. Will they be able to stop her and live life normally? https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3735188216 The gameplay is like that of old RPGs, where you explore a world map, travel from city to city, meet people, kill monsters, and upgrade your weapons.
67.15258: This game has won a huge number of awards and rightfully so. Many elements of the game are absolutely exceptional. The music is phenomenal, the story is compelling and poignant, the combat is frequently challenging enough to be engaging but not so challenging as to become monotonous through repetition. I loved the characters, I loved the story, I loved the music - I loved the experience of the game. The fights required enough skill and timing that beating the enemies felt rewarding to beat and the scaling was pretty well done for the first two-thirds of the game. The game isn't perfected though - it has some issues with pacing in the latter stages as you become far too strong if you don't push straight through to the main quest ending after about two-thirds of the game. The variety of builds also allow for you to become ridiculously strong and effectively break the game (although this isn't uncommon in the JRPG style combat systems).

67.15263: I came for the beautiful art direction. I stayed because the game emotionally parried me into depression. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of those rare RPGs that grabs your attention with its visuals and keeps you hooked with its characters, combat, and story. Every area looks like it belongs in a museum, every boss fight feels meaningful, and somehow the game manages to make "waiting for your turn" more exciting than some action games. The combat system deserves special praise. It takes traditional turn-based mechanics and injects them with active dodges and parries. Missing a parry feels bad. Landing a perfect parry chain makes you feel like the main character of an anime that got way too much budget. The story is fantastic and surprisingly emotional. I won't spoil anything, but let's just say this game had me staring at the credits while questioning my life choices and wondering why fictional characters keep hurting me more than real people.

70.16046: It's a great game, but exhaustingly huge. It's quite slow paced with MMO vibes, but the level designers did an amazing job to keep it interesting. Each map takes hours to complete, and they are all unique with many paths carved out (as opposed to being fully open and barren). Combat is fun, and while they give you a tactical camera that pauses time, I played on normal as I didn't want to faff around with that. Your companions are all nicely fleshed out with backstories, and the story has an interesting villain. The story otherwise takes a bit of a back seat - since the game is so large, you are expected to spend hours doing non-story things, and will be penalised by being underlevelled if you skip side quests. 74.16814: Dave the Diver is a simple yet engaging game. Gameplay is split into two parts, the diving and restaurant management halves, and both are well done. The diving part is the more interesting part, essentially you explore the depths, catching fish and having adventures. There's things you need to find in order to fulfill certain missions, and other things you need to retrieve to participate in research, that helps fund your activities. Money is used to upgrade your equipment and weapons, the latter of which you'll need in order to be able to survive the more aggressive creatures underwater. Of course fishing is very important if you want to do the following properly. Running the restaurant. You also have a sushi restaurant, and it's here you get your money to be able to upgrade your equipment and explore new areas. It's relatively simple, you need to serve the sushi and drinks to customers in time.
74.16815: Dave the Diver sure is a unique game. The characters are lovable, the storyline is engaging - despite being very cheesy at times -, and the gameplay is friendly to new and experienced gamers. It's a longer game than I'm used to, but it really progresses at the player's pace. Could I have completed it quicker.likely, but I enjoyed the freedom of not being rushed from task to task. The game's pacing felt very organic and player-driven. I was surprised by how many mechanics were present in the game; it felt like they were never-ending, which was a bit annoying at times. It was likely to keep engagement, but having new game mechanics introduced partway and late in the game felt like the developers were throwing pasta at the wall to see what stuck. Like, the gameplay was a little less established and cohesive. Overall, I really loved playing Dave and will be playing all the DLCs. It's a solid game, and I highly recommend it for anyone who's looking for something fun and quirky.

74.16929: **Dave the Diver — A Surprisingly Deep hidden pearl* Let me get this out of the way immediately: Dave is not your typical video game hero. He's a stocky, barrel-chested everyman who looks more at home at an all-you-can-eat sushi bar than plunging into the ocean depths — and I absolutely love him for it. In a medium obsessed with chiselled protagonists, Dave's portly frame is refreshing, charming, and oddly endearing. He waddles, he sweats, he huffs. He's *us*, and that's the point. But don't let the wholesome exterior fool you — Dave the Diver is a genuinely brilliant game, and it earns that praise across the board. The gameplay loop is deceptively simple: dive during the day, run a sushi restaurant at night. In practice, it becomes completely addictive. The diving mechanics feel weighty and satisfying, with real tension as you manage oxygen, depth, and an ever-growing arsenal of weapons and tools.

75.26300: All in all, Battlefield 2042 has been a real labour of love for me. The initial launch was remarkably underbaked, but I can’t deny the enjoyment that comes from firing a rocket launcher into a tornado. This may not be the best FPS multiplayer game available, and there are still plenty of issues that need ironing out, but there are occasionally some thrilling moments that you won’t be able to experience in the likes of Call of Duty or Fortinte. It remains frustrating having to pay full price for a multiplayer game, but if you’re already a fan of the franchise and don’t mind missing out on the campaign, you’ll likely enjoy yourself here. The nostalgic aspect of Portal mode will also draw fans in, and of course, the 4K graphics make it very pretty game, even if it has its cracks.

75.26322: What's really impressive in Battlefield 2042 is the variety that's on offer. Portal lets you relive the Battlefield games of the past, but on the 2042 side, DICE has cherry-picked from popular trends like hero shooters and battle royales. The best part is that, mostly, it has done a really effective job of curating those additions so that they bring more to what players already like about Battlefield, rather than change what already works.
75.26323: Battlefield 2042 is inconsistent. The maps and vehicular combat are top tier, while the specialists and redesigned scorecard diminish teamwork. Portal opens the window to what could be a brighter future for the franchise, and hopefully DICE adds meaningful updates to the service at a steady rate. Battlefield 2042 has a long and windy road ahead, and only time will define its lasting legacy. As of this moment, all but the most dedicated veterans should probably wait and see how things shake out.
75.26324: Battlefield 2042 is a fun enough time, but DICE needs to work hard if it wants to take the unrefined ideas found here and turn it into something that feels like a worthy successor to the Battlefield legacy.

75.26329: Overall, there isn’t much content to even write about with Battlefield 2042. The game is enjoyable, but it doesn’t do much to stand out from the last few iterations of the series and without a campaign, feels like it’s lacking in content. Hopefully some updates and adjustments can help clear up some of the issues I experienced, especially with the balancing in the Breakthrough mode. As it stands, if you’re looking for just more Battlefield, but with a different setting, this is a good option. If you’ve not been a big fan of Battlefield in the past, or at least in the recent past entries, I don’t think they’ve changed enough here to change your mind.

75.26332: Battlefield 2042 is an ambitious shooter that features the excellent Portal mode-creation tool, as well as a few, cool game types. Unfortunately, technical issues and balance problems mean that you may want to hold off buying the game until EA Dice irons out the kinks.
75.26333: There are some neat new toys while Portal delivers the series at its best, but 2042 launches as the weakest Battlefield in some time.
75.26334: Battlefield 2042 has a serious identity crisis. It clearly wants to be like Call of Duty: Warzone, with its overreliance on fast-quip Specialists that will serve as mannequins for endless cosmetic microtransactions. It also wants to grab some of the audience who religiously play Hunt: Showdown or Escape from Tarkov with its undercooked Hazard Zone mode. Finally, it also wants to be Battlefield to what’s left of a dedicated fan base that’s been left to watch the franchise chase the tail of its competitors for years. We loved Battlefield because it wasn’t Call of Duty or Counter-Strike or Fortnite or Apex or any other popular shooter. This mismanaged project clearly needed more time in the oven and a cohesive design that works to Battlefield’s strengths rather than a game attempting to be multiple things to multiple audiences. In a year where so many releases have been marred by a lack of polish and bugs, Battlefield 2042 may be the biggest offender.
75.26335: I really wanted to like it, but right now I see Battlefield 2042's little logo and I simply don't trust it. This game needs time. 78.17636: 바쁜 현대인을 위한 '유쾌하고 확률 없는' 폴아웃 혹은 폴아웃, 스카이림, 위쳐까지 모두 섭렵한 후에 비슷한 류의 게임을 찾다가 하게 되는 대체재. 혹시나 폴아웃과 비슷한 게임을 하고 싶어서 선택한다면. 폴아웃3나 뉴베가스를 이미 해봤다면 패스하는 것을 추천. 폴아웃4만 해봤다면 그럭저럭 할만할지도. 셋 모두를 해봤고 비슷한 재미를 찾다 보면 어쩔 수 없이 하게 될 게임. 좋은 말부터 하자면, 전투에서 동료에게 스킬을 지시할 수 있는 점이 재미있는 포인트. 이 기술들을 활용해서 내 체력이 부족해진 순간에 동료 스킬으로 몬스터의 어그로를 돌려서 위기를 넘길 수 있다. 폴아웃에서는 느껴보지 못한 신선한 감각인 데다가, 레벨링을 덜 해도 되는 이유로도 작동한다. 물론 중후반부에 가면 점점 센 적이 등장하기 때문에 완전히 레벨링으로부터 자유로운 것은 아니지만. 그 외에도 밝은 분위기와 화려한 색감의 월드를 돌아다니다 보면, 스카이림이나 폴아웃과는 전혀 다른 게임을 하고 있다는 게 실감난다. 단점이 치명적이라면 치명적인데, 몇몇 스토리를 제외하고는 최상의 시나리오로 플레이하는 게 너무 쉬워서 문제. 어느 한쪽 스탯을 높게 찍은 상태라면, 웬만해서 상황을 헤쳐나갈 수 있다. 왜냐하면 이 게임에는 확률이 존재하지 않기 때문이다. 위협을 하던 화술로 꼬드기던 요구 스탯보다 높기만 하면 프리패스라는 말이다. 그래서 그런지 선택으로 인해 발생한 결과가 크게 와닿지를 않는다. 오히려 선택지를 들여다보고 있다 보면 '이 선택지랑 이 선택지로 얘기하면 평화롭게 해결할 수 있는데, 얘네는 바보라서 이렇게 대립하고 있는 건가?'라는 생각이 들기도 한다. 폴아웃의 확률 선택지를 싫어했던 사람도, 이 게임을 하다 보면 그 시스템이 몰입과 성취감을 얼마나 많이 주는지를 재평가하게 될 것이다. 전반적으로 유쾌한 분위기로 흘러가다 보니 깊이도 함께 얕아져버린 것만 같은 게임. 확률이 없기 때문에 지루하긴 하지만, 폴아웃에 비해 짧은 시간 안에 자신이 원하는 엔딩을 볼 수 있다는 게 장점.

DLC로 갈수록 특히 심한데 이게 심지어 우주배경이라는 명목으로 배경음악까지 졸리다보니까 자꾸 졸게 된다. 폴아웃같은 경우 각종 등장인물들마다 저마다의 특색이 강하고 스토리와 깊게 연관되어 있어서 플레이하는 재미가 있다. 게다가 핵전쟁 이후의 나사빠진 세계관이라는 점에서 탐험하는 재미도 있는 반면에, 이 게임은 구현된 세계나 등장인물들이 개성이 너무 밋밋함. 그다지 특별할 것도 없는 설정을 찾아보는 재미도 없고, 탐험하는 재미도 매우 떨어지다 보니 뺑이치는게 너무 의미 없이 느껴진다. 무엇보다 그 미래세계관에 제대로된 투척무기조차 못던지는게 굉장히 이상하다고 생각한다. 과학 무기라는게 있기는 하지만, 그걸 제외하면 대체 미래의 기술력이 이정도밖에 안되나 싶을 정도로 김새는 무기들의 특성들도 그렇고, 그다지 구미도 안 당기는 개조 시스템도 한몫한다. 땜질로 무기의 데미지나 방어구의 방어도를 올릴 수 있는 건 좋다. 내가 원하는 무기를 계속 가지고 다닐 수가 있으니까. 물론 종류나 디자인도 별로 다양하지가 않아서 레벨이 조금만 높아져도 상위 버전의 아이템이 길바닥에 굴러다니니 주서 쓰는게 훨씬 편리하지만. 약물들이나 강화제도 직관성이 전혀 없다는게 문제다. 주인공이 글쎄 흡입기에다가 각종 술이나 음식을 쳐넣고 빨아들이는데, 뭐가 무슨 효과를 내는지 직관적으로 와닿지가 않는데다가 기능별로 분류도 안되서 하나하나 찾아내는게 짜증스럽다. 전체적으로, 충분히 매력적인 세계관을 구축해서 주인공이 우주를 탐험하는 재미를 충분히 느낄 수 있게 하는 게임이 될 수도 있었는데 매우 아쉽다는 생각이 든다.

78.17652: 요약 - AAA 게임이라고 생각하고 사면 10000000퍼 후회함, 세일하고 시간이 넘쳐날때 하루이틀 시간 태우기용 B급 JRPG 한편 산다는 느낌으로 사면 딱 좋음. 물론 캐릭터 와꾸는 JRPG가 아닌게 함정. (약스포) 본편 - 'SF장르가 처음'이라면 흥미로울 법한 스토리, 스토리는 괜찮았는데 하드난이도 기준으로도 전투가 도전적이라기 보단 짜증나는 경우가 많아서 결국 후반가면 동료스킬이니 근접스킬이니 다른거 세팅할 생각 안하고 화술스킬만 장인찍은다음 무지성으로 플라즈마 뿅뿅 난사하게됨. 일본 쯔꾸르게임 이후로 스토리를 보기위해 전투를 '민다' 라는 느낌이 드는 게임은 이게임이 처음이었음. 보스전을 하기 싫어서 설득스킬 맞추기 위해 옷작하고 도핑하고 동료퀘스트까지 깨면서 몸비트는 모습을 상상해 보았는가? 이게임 하다보면 그렇게 된다 시발. 고르곤의 위협 - 퀘스트라인이 노가다가 심하고 파면팔수록 나오는 내러티브도 적고 평이하기 때문에 그냥저냥 안해도 좋은 추가던전 같은 느낌이었음. 암튼 저가격은 아니니 할인할때 사든가 해라. 에리다노스 살인사건 - 걱정하지마라 모든 퀘스트를 깨고 모든 단말기를 뒤졌어도 범인을 못찾은 너는 절대 빡대가리가 아니다. 아니 이럴거면 추리 왜시켰노 시발련아. 결말빼고는 흥미로운 내러티브 때문에 재밌게는 했음, 스카이림에서 책한번 안펴본 사람이라도 에리다노스에 왔다면 밝은배경 속에서 사람들 곱창나는거 보고있다보면 절로 궁금증이 들어서 나처럼 모든 단말기와 문서를 뒤져보게 될 것이다.
78.17654: 재밌다. 널부러져 있는 개조부품과 총알들과 금고를 털다가 많은 친구를 잃었지만, 그래도 주머니 두둑한 황금고블린이 되었다. 매일 무겁게 기어다니지만 주머니에 비트 들어올때 기분이 히트를 치는 게임. 플레이타임은 제법 긴 느낌이다. 스토리모드로 금방 끝내려고 했는데 아직도 안끝나고, 끝날 기미만 보인다. 아무튼 SF좋아하면 추천함. 중간중간 영상미도 좋음. 한가지 팁을 주자면 싸우다가 동료가 죽어도 곧 다시 살아나니까, 전에 저장한걸 불러오기 할 필요가 없다. 불러오기 3번하고 중간에 동료가 살아나서 깨달음. 그리고 중간에 끼임 버그가 있는데, 새로 저장하고 다시 불러오면 알아서 빠져나온다.
78.17655: [h1]The Outer Worlds 리뷰 (스포일러 없음)[/h1] 총평 : 3 / 10 옵시디언 뽕에 빠진 나머지 폴아웃 뉴베가스의 유기적인 오픈월드와 방대한 스토리라인을 기대하고 플레이하면 많이 실망하실 겁니다. 트레일러에 속지 마십시오. 게임을 하면서 단 한순간도 트레일러에서 느낀 느낌을 받지 못했습니다. 제일 큰 문제로 플레이타임이 짧습니다. 돈값을 못합니다. [h1]그래픽[/h1] ☐ 현실과 같음. ☐ 아주 아름다움. ☑ 아름다움. ☑ 평범함. ☐ 나쁜 편. ☐ 눈 썩음. ☐ 기타 그래픽은 봐줄만한 편입니다. 노 맨즈 스카이보다는 훨씬 나은 그래픽인건 맞는데, 그렇다고 막 이쁘다고 할 정도의 그래픽은 또 아닙니다. 애시당초 출시일을 생각하면 그래픽에서 높은 점수를 주기는 애매한 것도 맞습니다. 전체적으로 억지로 형광칠을 한 느낌을 받을 수도 있는데, 저는 정말 외계 행성을 탐사하는 느낌이 들어서 괜찮았네요. 다양한 기후를 가진 행성이 등장한다는 점은 괜찮습니다. 다만 행성들의 크기가 크지는 않습니다. 그나마 메인 스토리의 중추인 스텔라 베이가 좀 크고 맵 구성도 다양한 편입니다. 각 탐험장소별 맵 디자인 자체는 나쁘지 않으나 탐험할 건덕지가 많이 부족하다고 느낄 여지가 충분합니다. NPC모션은 폴아웃 뉴베가스를 보는 느낌인데, 이게 익숙치 않으면 NPC들이나 적들의 모션이 상당히 어색하다고 느낄 수 있습니다. 개인적으로 폴아웃4보다 모션의 측면에서는 좀 더 별로였던 것 같네요. 여담으로, 우주선을 타고 자유탐사하는 행동은 구현되지 않았습니다. 우주선은 일종의 포탈로 기능할 뿐이며, 게임 완성도에 있어 마이너스 요소로 작용했습니다. [h1]스토리[/h1] ☐ 한 편의 영화. ☐ 우수함. ☐ 보통. ☑ 약간 부족함. ☐ 스토리를 스킵하는 것이 나음. ☐ 기타 스토리라인 자체는 재미있습니다. 그런데 문제는 너무 짧으며, 분기도 너무 단순하게 구성되어 있습니다. 이 뒤로 스토리라인이 더 생겨도 전혀 문제가 없을 것 같으나, 생뚱맞게 엔딩크레딧이 올라옵니다.
78.17656: 폴아웃같은걸 안해봤으면 나름 재밌게 즐길수 있는 게임 그리고 나는 아직 폴아웃을 플레이 안하고 했지
78.17657: 포장대비 내용물이 없고 소비할 컨텐츠도 없다
78.17658: 동료의 사랑만 이어주고 정작 본인은 생고생함.
78.17659: 짧은 플레이 시간동안 느낀점입니다. 1. 메스이팩트 할때의 행성간 이동의 설렘이 녹아들어있어 흥미로웠습니다. - 행성간 이동으로 동료를 얻고 같이 다니는 재미가 쏠쏠합니다. 2. 무기 특성이 올라갈때 무기 데미지가 오르지 않는 점은 아쉬웠습니다. - 레벨이 오를수록 고렙의 몬스터를 잡을려면 "땜질"을 통한 무기강화 이외에 순수 딜량을 늘릴 수 있는 수단이 없습니다) 3. 특정 무기 속성만 잘먹히는 플라즈마 망겜 - 보더랜드.. 같은 경우 "방깍" 속성의 무기가 없으면 고난이도 사냥터 진행이 어려운 경우가 있는데 양손무기(일반 속성) 들고 돌격했다가 한두방 맞고 쓰러지는 케릭터를 보며 실망이 좀 컸습니다.. 4. 게임 난이도가 올라갈수록 유리몸이 되는 동료들 - 쉽게 죽지 말라고 중갑옷을 둘둘 말아줘도 허구한날 쓰러지는 동료1, 동료2를 보면 한숨만 나오더라구요..
78.17660: 지루하네요. 전투도 별로고, 그냥 여기저기 돌아다니다보면 지금 뭐하는건지?
78.17661: 말은 웅장하고 화려하나 볼륨이 빈약함( 몹, npc 유닛의 갯수 등) 하지만 배경 색감은 좋아 기억에 남는게임
78.17662: 게임이 가지는 주제 때문에, 그리고 이러한 장르에 성공을 거둔 이전 다른 유명한 작품들이 있기에 플레이하면서 바이오쇼크와 폴아웃이 생각남. 그러나 둘을 합친 것 만큼 재밌냐? 그건 아님. 폴아웃처럼 자유롭지도, 바이오쇼크처럼 헤비한 주제를 잘 풀어나가지도 못함. 그래서 눈돌리고 그냥 아우터월드로 받아들이고 싶은데 도저히 그럴 수가 없음. 할인가에 사서 2만원에 9시간짜리 블랙코미디 영화를 본다고 치면 후회하지 않을 것 같은데, 머리속에 자꾸 더 재밌었던 이전 영화들이 생각나는 바람에 그게 안됨. 그러나 킬링타임용으로는 추천함. 딱 그정도로 재밌음.
78.17664: 쓰레기라고 단정짓기엔 나쁘진 않은 거 같고, 그렇다고 잘 만들었다기엔 뭔가 엉성한 구석이 많은 계륵 같은 게임이었다. 그 당시 할인가로 50%? 할인해서 31,500원에 산 걸로 기억하는데 매.긍에 걸맞는 게임인지 그냥 거품인지를 떠나서 내 취향은 아니어서 리스크를 감수하지 않기로하고 그냥 환불.
78.39470: 미묘. 선택에 따른 결과의 반영에서는 매우 우수하다. 하지만 전투는 액션임에도 불구하고 적의 명중률이 너무 높아서 사실상 그냥 발을 멈추고 서로 치고받으며 포션빠는 노잼 전투고, 아이템의 대부분은 쓰레기에 갑옷은 색만 바꾼 것들이 대부분, 무기도 조금만 진행하면 성능만 달라진 같은 무기로 도배된다. 동료들 디자인은 개성 0점으로 처음 만났을때 마을사람 A, B, C인줄 알았다. 짧은 플레이 타임도 단점으로 지적받는데 클리어까지 가지도 못하고 지루해서 그만뒀다.
78.39471: 이 게임은 결혼과 같다. 사기 전 잠깐 보고는 '와 씨, 사고(결혼 하고)싶다'하지만, 정작 사서(결혼해서) 몇 2시간(2년) 해보면(살아보면) 이 게임(사람)는 아니구나 라는걸 느끼게 된다. 개인적으론 스타크래프트가 더 재밌음.

78.39474: 총은 타격감이 없고 근접은 패는 맛이 있지만 너무 단조롭다 완성도 높은 디자인의 SF가상세계를 구경하는 맛은 좋았다 게임 진행이 생각보다 선형적인데 ( 길따라 가면서 - 몹 잡고 - NPC대화 패턴 ) 그 과정 속에서 세계의 생동감이 느껴지게하거나 흥미로운 이벤트가 없어서 지루했다 게임 초반에부터, 아직 충분히 몰입되지 않은 두 진영을 두고 선택을 강요해서, 초장부터 유쾌하진 않았던 기억 애초에 스토리 게임으로 플레이하려 시작했으나 스토리 몰입이 안됨 갑자기 냉동기계에서 깨워서 다짜고짜 이거해라 저거해라 초반 스토리 설계가 아쉽다 가장 아쉬운 점은 3인칭 안되는 점. 3인칭만 됐어도 그냥저냥 플레이 했을듯요 1인칭 게임 두번째 도전인데 쉽지않음 손발이 안보이니 걷는 것 같지가 않고 허공에 떠다니는 느낌이 들어서리 할튼 좋았던 기억보다 아쉬운 부분들이 더 많았어서 빨간버튼입니다
78.39475: 제 플레이타임이 보이시나요? 오리지날만 했을때 클리어 타임입니다. 그리고 저는 모든 DLC를 샀죠. 하지만 DLC를 할 마음이 들지 않습니다. 그냥 수집용으로 놔두려구요. 구매하시려는 분은 이가격에 이정도 시간만 즐기는것으로 만족스럽다 생각하시는 분만 구매하시면 되겠네요.
78.39476: 개발자들이 뉴베만든 짬이 있어서그런지 게임의 기본뼈대는 튼튼함 그래서 그런지 그냥 뉴배때 개발하면서 나온 장점들도 싹다 가지고 왔었으면 개인적인 바렘은 보더랜드 맵 여러개로 쪼개는것보다 그냥 큼직한 다양한 기후나 생태 행성하나에서 진행햇으면 어떨가 싶음 그리고 dlc 없으면 게임 생각보다 빨리 끝남

78.39480: 폴아웃4가 되고싶은 오픈월드 RPG 그러나 몰입감이 떨어지고 자막 읽기도 귀찮 군데 군데 자막이 없는 부분도 있음 63,000짜리는 아닌 듯
78.39481: 한 줄로 말하자면 (폴아웃과 바이오쇼크가 섞인듯한 감성) 그냥 심심할때 시간 때우기용으로 적절한 1인칭 RPG게임 하지만 그런 겜인거 치고 63000원은 선넘었다 해보고 싶다면 최소 60퍼이상 세일때 사는걸 추천 최고난이도인 슈퍼노바에 대해서도 말하자면 여지껏 최고난이도로 한 겜중에 아이템 파밍이 너무 쉬움, 메인 퀘만 밀어도 아이템을 아낄 필요를 못느낌 하지만 세이브는 함선아니면 그때 그때 저장이안되서 죽고나서 세이브포인트가 한참 전으로 돌아가니 귀찮음만 유발 차라리 파밍이 부족하거나 난이도가 더높고 세이브 포인트가 자주 있는게 더 날듯
78.39483: 동료 쾌 서브 쾌 포함 엔딩보는데 40시간 걸림. 가장 큰 장점은 스토리가 몰입하기 좋고 버그가 하나도 없음. 개인적으로 게임하면서 스트레스 하나도 안받고 재밌게 한 듯 할인할 때 사서 하면 후회할 일 없다고 생각함
78.39484: 캐릭터 디자인이 매력이 없는거를 넘어 특히 여성 캐릭터들 보면 진짜 게임 하기 싫어짐 다 중성화 수술 시켜놓은 듯. 여자인지 남자인지 구분은 할 수 있게 만들어놔야 되지 않을까? 진짜 몇번을 시도해봤는데 계속 보고있으면 정신병 걸릴거같은 캐릭터 디자인이라서 계속 끝까지 못 함.

78.39486: 오픈월드인데 뭔가 게임하면서 기분나쁜 오픈월드 로딩 천지에 유니크 무기 파밍하는 맛도 없고 매력도 없음 스토리도 뭔가 만들다만 스토리 dlc 까지 색깔만 다를뿐 똑같은몹 재탕에 맵도 작고 밀도도 낮음 사지 않는걸 추천
78.26450: The problem with this isn't that it is a bad game (far from it), but the fact that it failed to reach its true potential… or maybe the expectations were simply too high, because there's nothing here that anyone can point to and say that it is terrible. Sadly, there's almost nothing that's great either, apart from the role-playing element and the quality of writing. The gunplay? Ok. The exploration? Decent. The plot? Fine. The dominant feeling here is of a game that is good enough so that you won't hate it, but also not as good for it to be the flawless classic that it could definitely be - but again, that's probably those darn high expectations speaking, because flaws or no flaws, The Outer Worlds shouldn't be missing from any RPG collection.
78.26451: An excellent effort from Obsidian, and though The Outer Worlds doesn’t surpass its predecessors by offering a world worth visiting over and over, the adventure it presents is more than worth the time spent.
78.26452: Usually, a planet has just one or two settlements and a bit of wildlands to explore. But that’s for the best – instead of exploring miles of filler content, Outer Worlds keeps you moving from planet to planet, from one tense situation to another. [Issue#241, p.34]
78.26453: The Outer Worlds is an RPG with an incredible amount of choices to make, to the extent that it can sometimes feel more like an adventure game. While it becomes more linear near the end, there are few games that give the player this much freedom of choice.
78.26454: Obsidian set out to make a Fallout game, but didn’t think we’d mind if they actually made it a Firefly game along the way. So now we have an anti-capitalist Firefly mired in labor issues but elevated by rapidfire gunplay, peppered with chuckles from a tryhard sense of humor.
78.26455: The world may not remember it for years to come but here and now it’s worth giving it a chance – mostly because of the tragicomic atmosphere of the narrative, well fleshed out characters, and remarkable and funny dialogue. [13/2019, p.46]
78.26456: Obsidian could have easily fallen into the trap of creating a straight up Fallout clone, but the various planets in the Halcyon solar system and the types of quest available provides a good amount of variety, with excellent splashings of humour and moral dilemmas. It’s not breaking new ground, but it struts its stuff very well.

Practice mode alone has become an excellently robust training zone that clearly displays a lot of handy info about frame advantage and move properties. For pros, streamers and rank-chasers, the transfer to this sequel is therefore a no-brainer. And since little else quite like Tekken exists in the fighting game niche (don't listen, little Soul Calibur 3) the rest of us pugilistic rubes will only get FOMO if we don't follow. 86.26732: Tekken 8 is full of excitement and we loved it! Technically, in both substance and form, the Bandai Namco fighting game is a gem of the genre. Its new features in terms of gameplay are enough to stand out from previous opuses and hold its own against its competitors, all with vast content that is still substantial enough to play for dozens of hours. 86.26733: Tekken 8 is a marked improvement over Tekken 7 and a perfectly executed balancing act, keeping older players happy while revealing its trademark freedom to newcomers.
86.26734: Street Fighter 6 just raised the bar for AAA fighting games midway through 2023, and its long-time 3D rival Tekken has already matched it. Veterans can enjoy Tekken 8's new characters and mechanics without the game’s fundamentals being compromised, and a top-notch presentation will impress without technical hiccups. No one could have expected Tekken 8 to improve this much after Tekken 7 was already so strong, but it's clear that the new game won’t settle for anything less than being the series’ best.
86.26735: Tekken 8 takes everything that made its predecessors so popular and takes it to a whole new level.

87.26738: SFVI’s launch marks an impressive effort by Capcom, having learned from previous failings and while the lackluster World Tour mode and gross battle pass stains an otherwise spotless package, it still shines brightly as the new standard for fighters to come.
87.26739: For every great thing Street Fighter 6 does — and there’s a lot of them — there’s some flaw, some annoyance, or a ridiculous microtransaction system. If you’re looking for a 2D fighting game to play online or with your friends, Street Fighter 6 is one of the best around. But almost everything around the fighting itself is flawed in a way it probably shouldn’t be. The fight is all, but we shouldn’t have to deal with all of this other stuff to enjoy it.
87.26740: Street Fighter 6 is an undisputed masterpiece. From beginner-friendly game design to distinct visual combined with heavy hitting sensation, the overall experience was near perfect. In particular, World Tour mode gives you the unique feeling of Final fight meets GTA, have proved itself as a key content with respect for the original characters, tutorials and fun.
87.26741: Capcom learns from its mistakes and delivers one of the most fun Street Fighter games in the series' history.
87.26742: One of the best fighting games ever. Capcom has done magic with one of the most popular franchises in the world.
87.26743: A masterful addition to a legendary series that more than honors the momentous name it carries and will provide many, many hours of quality entertainment to anyone who decides to invest in it, whether they're a novice or a seasoned gamer.
87.26744: Street Fighter 6 is the complete package, with decades of refinement proudly on display. Whether you’re flying solo or hitting the streets with others, this is the definitive Street Fighter experience.
87.26745: As the series that pioneered fighting games, each new Street Fighter comes with weighty expectations. Street Fighter 6 confidently meets this hype, catering to neophytes and genre veterans by offering the most extensive array of offline offerings the franchise has ever seen alongside a flexible set of core systems and a diverse cast. Between its cohesive aesthetic, the bounty of clever features, and crisp central gameplay, it’s one of the most impressive entries the genre has seen in some time.
87.26746: Minor technical issues and questionable monetisation scuff what is otherwise one of the best fighting games we've seen in the last decade.
87.26747: Although the performance issues take the shine off things, I can still comfortably say Street Fighter 6 is the most fun I’ve ever had with any fighting game on release. After the disastrous launch that was Street Fighter 5, seeing Street Fighter back on top form again just feels right - and I’m extremely excited to see what the next year of content updates can do for a game that already feels this mechanically polished at launch.
87.26748: This is the first Street Fighter game in a long time where it feels like players of all skill levels are welcome. While World Tour mode is disappointing, the sheer scope of SF6 means you don’t need to wait for the inevitable Ultra Edition before jumping in.
87.26749: Street Fighter 6 is an exceptional entry in the franchise that reminds me why I love fighting games. Freshly introduced mechanics shake up the familiar dance of previous titles and notably improve the moment-to-moment gameplay. Capcom continues to demonstrate precisely how a team can triumphantly transform established IP. The blood, sweat, and style pouring from nearly every moment in Street Fighter 6 will delight newcomers and veterans alike.
87.26750: What speaks volumes about Street Fighter 6, in a sense, is the length of this review. It’s long, and yet I barely feel like I have scratched the surface. World Tour is a slightly ropey debut for a really strong single-player format – but SF6 is ultimately more than the sum of its parts, and the core fighting system alone justifies a high score and a strong recommendation. The previous entry launched with potential, but was racked with problems. This is a worldie from minute one. It’s a must-have. And it might just be the most compelling overall fighting game package of all time.
87.26751: Street Fighter 6 is the new milestone of the genre. A mass of content never seen in fighting games, two distinct single player modes and an experimental and innovative online component. All seasoned with a dry and harmonious combat system, perfectly balanced in every part. Capcom's latest effort is an essential purchase for anyone who wants to approach fighting games. So it's time to put on your kimono and step back into the ring: the King of fighting games is back!
87.26752: There’s something for everyone here. If you’re an old-school Street Fighter player like me, the game is alive and well, waiting for your return. If you’ve never really felt like fighting games were accessible to you, this might just be the game to welcome you in.
87.26753: Street Fighter 6 is open like never before, yet balanced enough to leave no one at ringside. In short, the set is superb and we can't wait to see what Capcom has in store for us for the follow-up to this nugget.
87.26754: Street Fighter 6 is the complete package and offers heaps of content, whether you're competitive or casual. World Tour is a surprisingly strong addition to the single-player experience, and the series has never been more approachable. If you ever wanted to 'get good' at a fighting game but never felt you had the tools, now is the time.
87.26755: The new incarnation of the historic Capcom series is exceptional in practically every aspect, a sort of extraordinary "mea culpa" for the problems of its predecessor at launch. The combat system is deep and layered - as well as offering a truly competitive option even for beginners - the tutorials are so complete that they represent a small encyclopedia of the genre, the single player modes will occupy hours of your time without effort, and the online competitive experience seemed more solid than ever. Negligible defects in the World Tour and a balance still to be defined are nothing at all, if faced with a title of this frightening quality.
87.26756: Street Fighter 6 succeeds in its ambition to cram some big things into one fighting game. Battle Hub may be silly, but it has a lot more personality and more to do than most other titles with their own online lobbies. Fighting Ground does a great job of showing off the new roster and improvements to the fighting engine, while placing an equal amount of attention on both offline and online players. World Tour makes for a somewhat nonsensical yet addictive adventure that can serve as a good basis for a full-fledged Street Fighter RPG. All of this is tied together with a presentation that does well in improving what came before it, only with more fidelity and flash. As stated at the beginning of this review, fighting game fans are going to have a good year, and Street Fighter 6 is an excellent component of that.
87.26757: Street Fighter 6includes everything you could want from a modern fighting game, and the mechanics at the game’s core are complete at the time of release. The World Tour campaign suffers from an uninteresting story and battles that feel like a slog, but overall, Street Fighter 6 will satisfy a wide range of fighting game fans.
87.26758: Full of content for all different types of gamer, whether that’s the one-vs-computer classic Street Fighter type or the player who loves to live online, making new pals. But underneath it all is an excellent fighting game that is as addictive as it ever was and a joy to play.
87.26759: Street Fighter 6 is a great game and it erases the bad memories Street Fighter 5 left in our memories. Although the World Tour mode is weaker than I expected, it is a great game that has managed to exceed my expectations in other aspects.
87.26760: Nice graphics, a mix of old and new mechanics and tons of cool little details make Street Fighter 6 the ultimate Street Fighter.
87.26761: It takes a lot to reinvent a 30-plus-year-old franchise while keeping step with tradition, and Capcom has succeeded admirably. Hopefully the still-to-come monetisation schemes are reasonable (details hadn’t been fully announced at the time of writing) and the netcode remains smooth, because the king of fighting games, Street Fighter II Turbo, is on notice: here comes a new challenger.
87.26762: Street Fighter 6 simplifies its gameplay systems without losing depth. It allows players to perform moves with just one button, providing a sense of freedom. It also features a replayable single-player mode that will attract casual gamers new to fighting games.
87.26763: Not content to keep its promises to hardcore gamers, Street Fighter 6 can be a good experience for neophytes. The game does, however, make a few mistakes, some forgivable given that it's a fighting game trying out new genres, or that a balancing patch can fix, and others less so, such as the lack of dubbing in some directions (even though the dubbers are generally good). The game may find it hard to get casual gamers to invest a little more, but whether it's a question of dosing out the online mode or having a good romp, the mission is accomplished and this opus has the weapons to bring everyone together around a complete versus fighting experience.
87.26764: Street Fighter 6 is further proof that Capcom is on top of the gaming world these days.
87.26765: Street Fighter 6 confirms a solid and formidable start. Whether it's your first fighting game or you're a lover of the genre, go for it.
87.26766: Street Fighter 6 represents the many lessons that Capcom learned from Street Fighter 5's rough launch. Its option-rich mechanics and community-centric features make it a fighting game that casual and hard-core players should look forward to.
87.26767: Capcom delivers a delightful fighting game with Street Fighter 6. The gameplay is top notch, the presentation is excellent, the game is well-stocked with modes, the roster is extensive, the online experience is flawless and we could go on and on. Every self-respecting gamer and fighting game enthusiast should get Street Fighter 6.
87.26768: Street Fighter 6 is a superlative fighting game with its robust online, amazing single-player content, gorgeous visuals, and sublime gameplay. It might be one of the best launch packages for any fighting game ever, and is a game of the year contender.
87.26769: Street Fighter 6 is the culmination of the experience CAPCOM introduced to the video gaming world back in 1987. With extremely solid gameplay mechanics, a wealth of excellent single-player content that teaches the basics in an extremely fun way, flawless online experience, amazing character design and attention to accessibility, Street Fighter 6 is in a league of its own, and one of the best fighting games in decades.
87.26770: Street Fighter 6 delivers a deep, complex, and satisfying fighting game bristling with fun new characters and an excellent multiplayer mode. Unfortunately, all of that's shackled to a truly terrible single-player RPG that stands as one of the most embarrassing things Capcom has released in years. If you're here for online play, you'll love it. If you want single-player action, stay far away.

99.22619: 구매를 망설이다가 구글 제미나이의 영업으로 늦게 구매했습니다. 이 분야의 최고점은 아직 슬더스라고 생각하고 있기 때문에 슬더스가 많이 언급 될 예정이니 이해 부탁드립니다. 구매 전에는 게임 시스템을 이해하지 못 하고, 슬더스 만큼의 전략성이 없는 거 아냐? 덱이 다양해봤자 얼마나 다양하겠어? 플레이어의 선택이 중요해? 억까 당하면 죽는거 아냐? 등의 생각들이 있었습니다. 구매 후의 인상은 이 게임은 단순히 카드를 잘 내는 게임이 아닙니다. 이 게임의 핵심은 조커라는 생각이 들었습니다. 조커는 게임 중 강력한 효과를 주는 슬더스의 유물과 유사한 포지션인데요. 다른 점이라면, 조커 카드는 슬롯 제한이 있다는 점입니다. 슬더스는 덱을 만드는 게임이라면, 발라트로는 조커를 만드는 게임이라고 할 정도로 이 조커 카드의 중요도가 높습니다. 결국 조커 카드가 뭐가 뜨냐에 따라 맞는 조합을 가고, 조커 카드에 맞춰서 포커 덱을 수정하고, 족보의 레벨을 올리는 게임이라고 생각합니다. 리플레이성은 슬더스랑 비교했을 때 살짝 아쉽습니다. 블루덱, 타로덱 등 스타팅 포인트를 약간 다르게 가져갈 수 있지만 이가 아이언 클래드, 사일런트급의 차이는 전혀 아니기 때문입니다. 결국 어떤 덱을 해도, 사용할 수 있는 전략의 폭은 거의 같기 떄문에요. 이 스타팅 덱은 단순히 승천작의 반복성을 위해서 라는 생각이 듭니다. 사실상 레드덱으로 깨나 블루덱으로 깨나 두 덱은 큰 차이는 없거든요. 하지만 기록에는 둘 중 하나만 찍히죠. 이를 목표로 잡는다면, 그 전까지는 계속해서 즐길 수 있을 것 같습니다. 슬더스의 가장 큰 매력 중 하나는, 몸을 비틀며 덱을 유연하게 가져가야하는 점이라고 생각합니다. 사일런트를 예로 들면 단도와 독이라는 상반되는 메커니즘을 섞어 먹어야하는 상황이 분명히 있죠. 발라트로는 특성상 이러한 재미를 주지는 못합니다. 그냥 어울리는 조커 고르면서 지금 쨀까? 아니면 세게 갈까? 등의 고민은 남아 있지만, 스트레이트와 포 카드 전략을 동시에 사용하기는 어려울 것입니다.
